role-prior-floors.reasoning: The pipeline runs build_forecasts.py, then complete_forecasts.py, then projection_model.py. In projection_model.apply (lines 601-607), game_floor and game_ceiling start as the previous forecast's values. They are replaced only when the player has 10 or more logs in 2024-25 plus 2025-26 (own quantiles, shifted to the new rate). The calibrated game_ratios(rate) branch runs only when game_floor is None or the player has no career features. So a player with a career record but fewer than 10 recent games keeps the v3 values from complete_forecasts. For these players complete_forecasts had no earlier forecast and took the no-f branch: floor = rates[10%] and ceiling = rates[90%] of the donors' season-average rates. That is one cross-player constant, which its own gameRangeBasis calls 'NOT a calibrated game P90'. It is never shifted to the new rate. The v4 output only applies min(rate, floor) and max(rate, ceiling). The result is that 190 of the 871 v4 forecasts share gameCeiling = 17.58 exactly. 12 of them are NBA-rostered (SOURCE_REPORTED). The floors are min(previous small-sample mean, 3.83). For version 4, the card in src/main.js:237 says 'Потолок матча — 90-й процентиль собственных матчей игрока за два сезона (у новичков — игроков того же уровня)', which is false for these players. src/season.js:372 uses (gameCeiling - gameFloor)/(2*Z90) as the per-game noise in pointsSpread. On 2025-26 games the constant ceiling is not a P90: it acts as P95 for 5-7 FP/G players and P84 for 9-11 FP/G players, and 29% of games fall below the 3.83 floor. game_spread stays at about P89-P90 at every level. The defect is real but immaterial to decisions. None of the 12 are on any FBL roster (DRAFT_PICKS or live league state). They project 5.6-10.4 FP/G, far below replacement level, and cost 1000-1100 or have no Sports.ru price. The per-game SD error is about ±1.5 FP. This is a correctness/labelling bug, not an owner rule question.

injury-double-count.reasoning:
Mechanism (src/season.js:93-99, 138-145, 151-164). expectedPoints gives each future game injuryFactor (0 before the ESPN returnDate) times chainCurve(h, share), where share = playRate = clamp(forecast.games/82, .5, .97). For ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED players, forecast.games is ESPN's projected games alone (projection_model.py:586, the owner's call). When ESPN has already priced a known long absence into its total, the report zeroes those games a second time, and the already reduced season share then applies again to the games after the return.

ESPN does price old, long injuries, and the data show it. Butler 39 (ACL, back 2027-01-02), Sharpe 27 (meniscus since 08-24), DiVincenzo 4 (Achilles) and Moody 12 (patellar tendon) are impossible as healthy totals. Fresh injuries are NOT priced: Furphy (ACL diagnosed 10-19), Gueye, Strawther and Claxton have the same ESPN games in the 2026-10-17 snapshot (data/forecast-snapshots/2026-27/2026-10-17.json) as in today's 10-20 fetch (61/70/66/69). For those players the current code is correct.

So the double count is real for the priced subset only. F080's "any injured player understated 15-35%" and its critical severity are overstated. A blanket fix (share = G/gamesAfterReturn for every reported player) over-corrects fresh injuries. It would newly flag Claxton as an injured target for teams 6 and 7 (+72/+97 season), which is probably wrong. The 0.5 clamp also distorts the priced cases the other way: Moody 12 becomes 31 games, overvalued by about 200 FP.

The in-season part of F080 (playRate counts the missed games of the current spell, and then the report zeroes the rest of the spell) is only partly supported. My backtest of 160 returns from spells of 10+ games (2024/25 and 2025/26, single-club players): the code's flat playRate at the return has bias -0.099 / MAE 0.267, the spell-excluded rate +0.097 / 0.230, the prior alone +0.107 / 0.279. The chain uplift after a healthy restart is ignored here. So the code is somewhat pessimistic and the proposed exclusion over-corrects. This part is not active today (no games played yet).

Decision impact today: none of the 8 current Sports.ru rosters holds an Out player, and injuredTargets returns nothing for any team, both with the current code and with the threshold fix below. The error sits in displayed season values (transfer cards, explainSwap, injured targets) and in future decisions when a priced long-term injured player is a buy/sell candidate. This is a model calibration choice, not a league rule, so no owner decision is needed.

injury-double-count.reasoning:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced it. The auditors still overstate it today, most of their pre-season examples are wrong, and their blanket fix would do harm.

How the code works:
- chainCurve (src/season.js:104-118) solves for the hazard scale so that the chain, started healthy, plays a share `share` of 82 games. Its input should therefore be a healthy-start season share.
- expectedPoints (season.js:151-164) skips every game before the ESPN returnDate (injuryFactor=0). It then restarts that healthy chain at the return, using share=playRate.
- Any part of the reported absence already inside `share` is therefore subtracted a second time. This happens through two channels.

(1) Pre-season channel (F016/F096/F137): share = forecast.games/82, and forecast.games is ESPN's alone for ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED players (projection_model.py:587).
- Real only where ESPN's total already prices the absence. To tell which, I compared ESPN games with the model's games, scaled by the median ESPN/model ratio of the 264 ESPN players with no report (1.124).
- Priced (residual is strongly negative): long injuries known for months. DiVincenzo -66 (out 74 club games), Moody -54, Sharpe -36, Butler -10 (his model 44 already starts 'endedOut').
- Not priced (residual 0 to +29): absences reported in October. Porzingis +13, Claxton +3, Strawther +3, Gueye +3, Nurkic +13, Strus +29, Beal +16, Furphy +6 (ESPN 61 is more than the 48 games left after his return).
- So the code is right for most of the examples the auditors list. Their rule (share = G/gamesAfterReturn for every injured ESPN player) would overvalue Porzingis by about 236 FP and Claxton by about 117 FP. On today's data it also creates a spurious 'buy Claxton' injured target for teams 6 and 7.
- The pre-season double count is material for Butler (-299 FP, 25.4 vs 39.8 games) and Sharpe (-109 FP). DiVincenzo and Moody are masked by the 0.5 floor on the share (a separate issue, raised in F137).

(2) In-season channel (F080), which is larger. playRate is a per-game Beta-binomial update with k=20, and it counts every missed game of the reported spell as evidence.
- After the return the report disappears, so the whole spell keeps weighing on the post-return chain.
- ACCEPTANCE.md:98 says 'No recency weight, so the injury report is not a second penalty for a current absence'. That claim is false for long spells.
- Returns in 2024/25 and 2025/26 (213 spells of 10+ games, single-club players): the actual post-return share played was .559 / .543 / .635 for spells of 10-20 / 20-35 / 35+ games. playRate at the return gave .461 / .389 / .222, and the chain adds back only about .03-.05.
- Dropping the spell's games entirely gives .609 / .639 / .55. That is much closer but overshoots on medium spells, so the right fix sits in between: a spell should count as one event, not as N misses.

This is not an owner decision. The owner's call is 'games are ESPN's', not how a reported return is reconciled with them, and ACCEPTANCE explicitly claims the double penalty does not happen.

Why high and not critical:
- Today no FBL roster holds an Out player (only Day-To-Day players with return 10-21).
- The narrowly correct pre-season fix flips no current advice.

verdict-band.reasoning:
transferVerdict (src/season.js:312-323) labels a transfer that has already been made by comparing its expected month and season gains with a fixed T=15 FP. It never looks at uncertainty. The confidence machinery in the same file (pointsSpread/explainSwap, plus CONFIDENT=.7 and DOUBTFUL=.6 at line 365) is used for advice but not here. On current data, one swap has a season SD of 439-775 FP and a month SD of 85-148 FP. A ±15 band is therefore about ±0.03 SD on the season, so 'even' almost never fires (0 of 20 real transfers) and coin-flip moves get firm labels. Examples: 'LeBron James > Anthony Davis' gets '💪 Усиление' at P(gain>0) 58% season and 59% month. 'Tyler Herro > Onyeka Okongwu' gets '🤡 Ослабление' at 54% and 56% against. 'Isaiah Hartenstein > Egor Demin' gets 'Ослабление' with a season gain of -1 FP (50%). Only 7 of 20 labels reach the tool's own 70% CONFIDENT level on the season horizon, and 6 of 20 are below 60%. The advice engine would call the same move 'сомнительно', so the two outputs contradict each other.

Why low and not high: the labels appear only in the owner's private Telegram notifier (rival-transfer and own-transfer messages). transferVerdict is not imported by the UI or by league-feed. The numeric gains are printed next to the label. The actionable 'Тебе: …' advice in the same message is already gated by explainSwap confidence (CONFIDENT/DOUBTFUL), so no transfer decision or FP depends on the verdict. Its expected-value direction is not wrong either: a +139 FP expectation is an upgrade in expectation. The defect is a misleading certainty in commentary, not a wrong decision.

Side claims:
- 'Spreads are not calibrated as the docs claim': refuted as stated. ACCEPTANCE.md lines 119/147/156 openly report 72-74% coverage of the 80% range. That is a separate calibration topic, not part of this fix.
- 'Game noise dominates a one-week horizon' (pointsSpread comment): measured median game-noise variance share is 0.50 (IQR 0.42-0.60) on today's week horizon. The comment overstates it, but the share grows as in-season games shrink the prior term, so this is immaterial.

verdict-band.reasoning:
The arithmetic is right: ±15 FP is small next to the swap SD from explainSwap. The finding's conclusion does not follow from it, and the fix it proposes is worse than the current code.

1) What the label says. transferVerdict (src/season.js:312-323) gives the sign of the expected gain. It compares playerOutlook means over 4 weeks and over the season, and uses ±15 FP as the house threshold for a material change; acquisition and marketAlerts use the same 15 as minGain. This is the documented design: ACCEPTANCE.md:111 says "a season gain decides a verdict first", an injured player bought for the season is "a season investment", and tests/season.test.js:187-195 locks this in ('down' for a 30→20 FP/game swap, 'even' for 30→31). FBL standings are total FBL points, and points add up. So for "did this move make their team stronger in expectation?", the expected gain is the right quantity. Telegram always prints the magnitude beside the label (notify-transfers.mjs:113/124 + telegram-format gains()), for example "📈 Им: +139 ФО за сезон · +32 за 4 нед. · 💪 Усиление". For the owner's own moves it is also prefixed "По модели".

2) The wrong yardstick. explainSwap.confidence is P(realised gain > 0) under the full spread of outcomes: the calibrated season range, which includes injuries and games missed, plus game-to-game noise. That is outcome risk, not the chance that "stronger in expectation" is wrong. My decomposition shows game noise is only about 5% of season variance. With game noise alone, every |s| ≥ 124 move has P ≥ 0.88. The 0.55-0.65 values therefore come from the season-range term, which is mostly availability and injury risk that cannot be known in advance. A label about expected value should not be rewritten into one about outcome probability. "The even band is hit 2-3% of the time" is likewise the chance that a realised outcome lands within ±15. The verdict never uses that quantity.

3) The proposed fix does harm. Gating on P_season ≥ 0.70 / ≤ 0.30 on the current data turns 13 of the 20 real transfers into "🤷 Примерно равноценно". Ten of them have |season gain| ≥ 124, including Embiid>Kawhi +285, Buzelis>LeBron +238/+80, Knueppel>Okongwu −209 and White>Knueppel +207. Calling those "roughly equal" is a false statement about expected value. It would hide exactly the rival threats the finding wants to show. The 0.25·sd band also relabels LeBron>AD (+139/+32) as "even".

4) The threshold does not matter in practice. With today's live snapshot all 20 labels are directional (10 up, 10 down). A much coarser ±50 season / ±25 month band changes only 3: Embiid>Kawhi and George>Edey move from up to long because their month gain is exactly +25, and Fox>Pritchard (−41/−23) moves from down to even.

5) It drives no decision. The label is used only in the two notifier messages. Whether to grab the player a rival released is decided by decide(), which has its own CONFIDENT=0.7 gate and says "🤔 можно взять, но не уверенно" below it. That fits "upgrade in expectation, uncertain" and does not contradict it.

6) The side claims are overstated or wrong:
- (a) Calibration: holdout coverage80 is 0.746 (projection-report-only.json) and 0.740 (projection-model-audit.json). That implies an SD factor of 1.12-1.14, not 1.19; the 72% figure is the older ACCEPTANCE.md:119 line. ACCEPTANCE reports the shortfall openly (lines 119/147/156), and the misses are asymmetric (above 15%, below 11%). Verdicts do not use the SD at all, so no label can change.
- (b) "Game noise dominates a one-week horizon is false": game noise is a median 56% of week variance (p10 0.32, p90 0.75), and over 50% for 62% of 456 players. The comment holds.

What is left is presentation only: the label shows no confidence, and the same absolute 15 FP applies to 4 weeks (about 1 FP/game) and the season (about 0.2 FP/game). That is an optional UX tweak (for example appending the season %), not a math error or a defect.

objective-pfirst.reasoning:
The math in the cluster holds up. What it means for decisions today is much smaller than the auditors claimed, and the objective itself is a league-owner choice, not a code defect.

1. Code confirms the objective. The draft scores players with riskAdjustedValue = slotSeason/82 - 0.14*(mean - floor)/82 (src/valuation.js:32-37, 'balanced' style). That feeds plan.js:66, the bots (simulation.js:37), main.js:296 and insights.js:8, which Telegram uses through notify-transfers.mjs:65. The season optimiser bestPackage (src/season.js:268-318) maximises expected playerOutlook points and has no variance or rank term. The season tab shows the place as a point estimate only (src/season-ui.js:413-414).

2. Variance really does raise P(1st), for every team. I used the app's own sampler (scenarioSeasonScore) on the real 80-pick rosters with common random numbers over 60k runs. I compared adding zero-mean noise of sd 500 (team sd +82..94) against adding +100 FP of mean. One FP of team sd is worth 0.48 / 1.04 / 1.00 / 0.60 / 1.37 / 1.57 / 1.31 / 1.04 FP of mean for teams 1..8. This matches F113's 0.48-1.43. So a downside penalty applied to everyone has the wrong sign if the prize is 1st place. The 'balanced' penalty is 50/74/103 FP (p10/p50/p90) over the top 120 players.

3. Why the impact is small now:
- (a) The draft ended on 18.10. DRAFT_PICKS has 80 entries and the app's draft state was complete. So the plan, the ФО* column, the alternatives and the bots no longer drive a real decision. Their only live use is the 'value per 1000' pros/cons text in cards and Telegram.
- (b) The UI already discloses the adjustment. main.js:328 says '*ФО в списке — прогноз сезона с поправкой на риск'. A code comment calls the style a preference. F113's 'math-error' label is therefore too strong.
- (c) The auditor's own replay found the balanced and risk-neutral now-picks identical at 10 of 10 real picks.
- (d) For the 21 real transfers recorded in live-league-state.json, the P(1st) variance adjustment converts to a median of 39 FP of mean (max 125). The median |expected season gain| is 259 FP, and the adjustment flips the direction of 0 of 21 transfers. It could only reorder near-tied packages, and late in the season for teams far from 1st (F029). Neither case is validated.
- (e) Which objective is correct depends on the prize structure: P(1st), expected place, or top-3. Under expected place the value of variance is about 0 at season start. Nothing in data/league-rules.json or docs says what the prize is, so the owner has to decide.

objective-pfirst.reasoning:
The math in the findings is right in direction but too narrow. On current data, team variance does raise P(1st) for all 8 teams. Calling the draft penalty a "math-error" (F113, high) does not hold up, for four reasons.

(1) The penalty is a documented design choice, not an accident. src/valuation.js:32-33 says "A style only states a preference about the downside", docs/SCORING_AUDIT.md:52 says the same, and main.js:328 tells the user that the plan's ФО are "с поправкой на риск". The UI does not hide it.

(2) The sign of the "correct" risk preference depends on the prize structure, and that structure is not recorded anywhere: league-rules.json, ACCEPTANCE and the docs have no prize or payout fields. On the current post-draft rosters, using the app's own sampler (scenarioSeasonScore, 60k common-random-number draws), the value of 1 FP of team sd in FP of mean is:
- P(1st) objective: +0.42 for the owner's team 0, the favourite.
- Top-3 objective: -0.35 for team 0.
- Expected place: -0.38 for team 0.
- Weaker teams: positive under every objective.
So for the user's own team the downside penalty fits expected place and top-3, and goes the wrong way only if just 1st place counts. The claim that "no rank-based objective supports the penalty" is false for the team the app advises.

(3) The magnitude is small. The penalty is a median 5.3% of slot value (p10-p90 3.9-7.7%) in the top 120. It reorders 28% of near-neighbour pairs, but only where raw gaps are 43 FP or less, so near-ties only. The auditor's own replay found the now-pick identical under balanced and risk-neutral at 10 of 10 picks.

(4) The draft finished on 18.10.2026, so plan.js and the MILP no longer drive any 2026/27 decision. The season optimizer (bestPackage, recommendation) is already risk-neutral on expected FP, with a season-not-lowered constraint. The Telegram 'value per 1000' cue uses riskAdjustedValue, but a near-proportional 5% shift barely moves its percentiles.

The in-season angle (F029) is real but objective-dependent too. A swap from median to p90 player spread (sd 401 to 558) changes team sd by about 59 FP, worth about ±25 FP for team 0 depending on the objective. Swaps at the extremes are worth about ±35 FP. This matters mostly late in the season, and the static model ignores the 75 future transfers each team has.

F036 (no P(place) in the season tab) is a feature request. It also runs against a documented stance: SCORING_AUDIT.md:3 says random first-place shares were deliberately removed from primary recommendations, and ACCEPTANCE:20/53/61 says model first-place shares are not win probabilities. The deterministic table is not wrong. "Прогноз" is a point forecast, and the top two (28.0% vs 24.3% P1 on current data) are indeed close.

F123 is a wording nit. The Wilson interval correctly measures Monte-Carlo error of the model's share. The note under the table already says it is not a win probability, but the tooltip "95% доверительный интервал" can be misread as uncertainty about winning.

Overall the issue is real as an improvement and a disclosure point, immaterial to current decisions, and its core depends on an owner decision.

That makes Availability.distribution bisect the hazard scale c in [e^-6, e^6] until the chain's mean equals ESPN's number. A mean of 82 out of 82 is only possible with zero hazards, so c drops to e^-6 and the pmf becomes a point mass at 82. Targets of 77-81 push c to 0.1-0.25 and squeeze the lower tail. chain-anchor-degenerate.reasoning:
The core math holds. apply() sets games = ESPN games (the owner's call, PR #61, 22a494a, 20.10) and calls with_games(p,chain,...,games,healthy). Availability.distribution then bisects the hazard scale c over [exp(-6), exp(6)] until the pmf mean equals that target. When the target equals the season length L=82, the only distribution that can have mean L is a point mass at L, so the degenerate range is forced, not a numerical quirk. c hits the exp(-6)=0.0025 floor and the pmf puts 98% on 82. Targets of 77-81 force c to about 0.03-0.2, which takes out most of the spread.

ESPN's number is a point projection, and nothing calibrates it as a mean or a ceiling: there is no archive of ESPN projections, and the holdout coverage of 79.6% only covers regression-anchored pmfs, never ESPN-anchored ones. So the published 80% ranges for high-ESPN players are not validated. An empirical proxy shows they are far too narrow. Among healthy starters (played the club opener) who had 80+ games the season before (n=86), the next season had mean 71.3, q10 51, P(82) 16%. With 80+ games in both previous seasons (n=16): mean 77.4, q10 65, P(82) 44%. The chain anchored at ESPN 82 gives q10 82 and P(82) 0.98. Even Bridges (82 games in 5 straight seasons) does not justify 98%. Champagnie (17/74/80/82) and Carrington (81/82) clearly do not.

The owner's decision covers the point estimate only (it was made so the assistant stops selling healthy stars), not the range shape. So decoupling the pmf shape from the published games is a calibration fix, not a rule change. The pre-#61 anchor (model+ESPN)/2 is still described in ACCEPTANCE line 155 ("regression, or its mean with ESPN"). It gives q10 of 66 (Bridges) and 56-61 (ESPN-77 players), close to the empirical proxy.

Several parts of the finding are overstated:
- shortSeasonRisk near 0 is about right. The empirical P(<21 games) is 0-1.2%, and the UI warning fires at 20%, so no warning is lost under any anchor.
- The unattainable-target case (Podziemski 79 and Knueppel 78 giving pmf mean 76.8) is a 1-2 game gap that errs on the conservative side.
- The auditor's proposed fix "w fitted by log score of actual games" is impossible, because no ESPN archive exists.
- The decision impact is small. The draft is over, the in-season chainCurve re-fits the hazards to the in-season share anyway, and the confidence effect is under 1 pp.

What is left is materially miscalibrated displayed probability claims for a defined group: about 30 players, 9 of them on FBL rosters. Medium, not high.
